content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of baked or boiled chicken or turkey served with vegetables: carrots, broccoli and/or dark‑green leafy greens (spinach, kale, cabbage). It contains no potatoes or sauces, making it low‑calorie and nutrient‑dense.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are excellent sources of lean protein.
Broccoli provides more than 100% of the daily value of vitamin C per 100 g.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Leafy greens, especially kale, contain more calcium than milk.
Excluding potatoes lowers the glycemic index of the meal.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Poultry meat supplies all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: White meat contains little saturated fat, which is beneficial for cardiovascular health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both the meat and carrots provide niacin, vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Broccoli and leafy greens are rich in polyphenols and vitamin C, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fiber and minerals
items.content: The vegetables add dietary fiber, potassium, magnesium and iron, supporting digestion and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken or turkey proteins.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Undercooked meat can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; ensure internal temperature reaches 75 °C.

items.title: Excess vitamin A
items.content: Large amounts of carrots may lead to hypervitaminosis A in sensitive people.

items.title: Oxalates in leafy greens
items.content: People prone to kidney stones should moderate intake of kale and spinach due to high oxalate content.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the meat by boiling, baking, or steaming, then slice into strips. Steam or lightly sauté the vegetables to retain crunch and nutrients. Serve warm, optionally garnished with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared dish in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 75 °C before serving.
